title: Generate PowerPoint Presentations from Data
text: prestr R package helps go raw data presentation-ready PowerPoint minutes. Whether ’re reporting results, summarizing findings, building slides meeting, prestr handles heavy lifting. package provides three core functions: create_ppt_report() : Generate .pptx file title slide data table auto_chart() : Create bar, line, scatter charts data frame summarize_insights() : Extract key statistics numeric columns

title: Generate PowerPoint Presentations from Data
text: can install prestr directly GitHub:

title: Generate PowerPoint Presentations from Data
code: library(prestr)  data(sales_data)  create_ppt_report(   data        = sales_data,   title       = "Monthly Sales Report",   subtitle    = "Q1 - Q4 Performance",   output_file = "sales_report.pptx" )

title: Generate PowerPoint Presentations from Data
code: library(prestr)  data(sales_data)  # Filter to one category electronics <- sales_data[sales_data$category == "Electronics", ]  auto_chart(   data       = electronics,   x          = "month",   y          = "sales",   chart_type = "line",   title      = "Electronics Monthly Sales" )

title: Generate PowerPoint Presentations from Data
code: library(prestr)  data(sales_data)  summarize_insights(sales_data) #>      column   min    max     mean  median #> 1     sales  2900  28900  10564.58  8500 #> 2    profit   700   9100   2916.67  2350 #> 3 units_sold    58   815    306.46   272

what: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
title: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
text: Creates styled ggplot2 chart data frame. Supports bar, line, scatter chart types. returned object can customized standard ggplot2 functions passed create_ppt_report().

title: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
code: auto_chart(data, x, y, chart_type = "bar", title = NULL)

title: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
text: data data frame least one row one column. x single character string naming x-axis column. Can type. Must exist data. y single character string naming y-axis column. Must exist data must numeric. chart_type One "bar", "line", "scatter". Defaults "bar". title optional character string chart title. Defaults NULL.

title: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
text: ggplot object styled theme_minimal(). Can printed, modified, saved ggsave().

title: Auto-Generate a Chart from a Data Frame — auto_chart
code: df <- data.frame(Category = c("A", "B", "C"), Value = c(10, 25, 15))  # Bar chart (default) auto_chart(df, x = "Category", y = "Value")   # Line chart with title auto_chart(df, x = "Category", y = "Value",            chart_type = "line", title = "Trend") #> `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation. #> ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?   # Scatter plot auto_chart(df, x = "Category", y = "Value", chart_type = "scatter")

what: Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
title: Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
text: Generates PowerPoint presentation (.pptx) data frame. output includes formatted title slide data table slide displaying provided data. Useful quickly turning analysis results presentation-ready output.

title: Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
text: data data frame include presentation. Must least one row one column. title single character string used presentation title. output_file single character string specifying output file path. Must end .pptx. Defaults "report.pptx". subtitle optional single character string title slide subtitle. Defaults NULL (subtitle shown).

title: Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
text: Invisibly returns file path saved .pptx file.

title: Create a PowerPoint Report from a Data Frame — create_ppt_report
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ df <- data.frame(   Category = c("A", "B", "C"),   Value    = c(10, 25, 15) ) create_ppt_report(df, title = "My Report", output_file = "my_report.pptx") } # }

title: Monthly Sales Performance Data — sales_data
text: dataset containing monthly sales performance metrics across four product categories one year. Useful demonstrating create_ppt_report(), auto_chart(), summarize_insights().

title: Monthly Sales Performance Data — sales_data
text: data frame 48 rows 5 variables: month Month name (e.g., "January") category Product category: Electronics, Clothing, Food, Furniture sales Total sales dollars profit Total profit dollars units_sold Number units sold

title: Monthly Sales Performance Data — sales_data
code: data(sales_data) head(sales_data) #>      month    category sales profit units_sold #> 1  January Electronics 15200   4200        152 #> 2 February Electronics 13400   3800        134 #> 3    March Electronics 16800   4900        168 #> 4    April Electronics 14200   3900        142 #> 5      May Electronics 17500   5100        175 #> 6     June Electronics 19200   5800        192 summarize_insights(sales_data) #>       column  min   max     mean median #> 1      sales 2900 28900 10395.83   8150 #> 2     profit  700  9100  2863.54   2050 #> 3 units_sold   58   815   291.27    263

what: Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
title: Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
text: Computes summary numeric columns data frame, returning key statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, median numeric variable. Useful quickly extracting insights building presentation create_ppt_report().

title: Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
text: data data frame least one numeric column. round_digits integer specifying number decimal places round numeric results . Defaults 2.

title: Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
text: data frame one row per numeric column containing: column Name numeric column min Minimum value max Maximum value mean Mean value median Median value

title: Summarize Key Insights from a Data Frame — summarize_insights
code: df <- data.frame(   Category = c("A", "B", "C"),   Sales    = c(100, 250, 175),   Profit   = c(20, 80, 55) ) summarize_insights(df) #>   column min max   mean median #> 1  Sales 100 250 175.00    175 #> 2 Profit  20  80  51.67     55 summarize_insights(df, round_digits = 0) #>   column min max mean median #> 1  Sales 100 250  175    175 #> 2 Profit  20  80   52     55
